title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 718–720 of the continuation of La Longue Marche): Grothendieck has been studying homomorphisms from the profinite modular group (SL(2,Z)^ ≅ π1(M_{1,1}), and its quotient by ±1) to groups G_{p,σ} built from the abelianized (Fermat) tower of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. On the previous page he looks for a geometric, 'Fermat-tower-like' interpretation of such a homomorphism. This page sets up that interpretation.

(1) He identifies the relevant fundamental group with π1(M'_{1,1}). Here M'_{1,1} is the modular scheme (really a stack) over Q of elliptic curves 'à symétrie près', i.e. modulo the automorphism −1. Its π1 is SL(2,Z)^/±1. Equivalently it is the moduli of 'quasi-elliptic curves' X̃ = X/±1: a P^1 with a marked point (the image of the origin) and an étale degree-3 divisor (the images of the 2-torsion points).

(2) Observation: the Fermat tower can be made to vary over an arbitrary base S of characteristic 0 carrying such an X̃.
- Let p: S' → S be the degree-3 finite étale cover given by the points of order 2 of X̃.
- Put M_0(X̃/S) = p_*(Z_{S'})/Z_S (formula 299). This is a twisted constant Z-module, locally free of rank 2; he corrects 'trois' to 'deux'.
- Put M_1(X̃/S) = M_0 ⊗_Z Ẑ(1), with Ẑ(1) = T_∞(G_m) (formula 300). This is a profinite locally constant coefficient system, locally isomorphic to Ẑ^2.
- Fibrewise, M_1 is exactly H_1 of P^1 minus the three 2-torsion points, i.e. the Galois group of the maximal abelian (Fermat) pro-cover. It is generated by the three inertia classes with sum zero, hence the quotient Z^D/diagonal; this matches the classical μ^3/μ(diagonal) for Fermat curves.
- M_1 is functorial in X̃/S for isomorphisms and base change, i.e. it is a cartesian section of a suitable fibred category over the moduli stack.

(3) The next page states the goal. A 'Fermat tower' over the moduli is the datum, for every X̃/S, of an M_1(X̃/S)-torsor F_∞(X̃/S), compatible with isomorphisms and base change. A natural candidate is the fibre of the abelian pro-cover over the fourth marked point, the image of the origin.

The preceding theorem says such an F_∞ exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism, once one requires that the induced map Π_{03}^∧ → M^∧ be the canonical one.

He then proposes a second construction. Take the generalized Jacobian J of an elliptic curve X/S with modulus the 2-torsion multisection S' ⊂ X. Its degree-0 part J^0 is an extension of X by the torus R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m. That torus has cocharacter group p_*Z/Z = M_0, so its Tate module is exactly M_1. The torsor would then come from the Kummer/Tate theory of this extension.

The overall aim is to geometrize the homomorphism π1(M_{1,1})^ → G_{p,σ}: Galois/modular action on the Fermat tower as monodromy of a family of tori or generalized Jacobians over the moduli of elliptic curves.
errors: Rank: p_*Z/Z has rank 2, and Grothendieck himself corrects 'trois' to 'deux'.

The quotient (not the kernel) of p_*Z by the diagonal is the right model for H_1(P^1 − 3 points) and for the Fermat Galois group μ^3/μ. The two choices (quotient vs kernel) differ integrally at 3 (an index-3 sublattice question), so the choice matters over Ẑ.
Gap: the page does not specify the base point or normalization used to rigidify the torsor. This is supplied on the next page by the uniqueness condition on Π_{03}^∧ → M^∧.

Notational ambiguity: 'M_{0,3} = M'_{1,1}' only makes sense as an orbifold/stack identification, consistent with the earlier 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧} ≅ SL(2,Z)^/±1. The rigid M_{0,3} is a point, so his index convention differs from the modern one.

ideas.what: Fermat tower = maximal pro-abelian cover of P^1 minus 3 points, with Galois group Ẑ(1)^3/diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower / abelianized π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986), Anderson (1989), Coleman; classical Fermat curves

ideas.what: Relative (twisted) Fermat tower over a base S: the coefficient system M_1 = (p_*Z_{S'}/Z_S) ⊗ Ẑ(1) attached to the étale triple of 2-torsion points of an elliptic curve modulo ±1, as a cartesian section over the moduli stack M_{1,1}/±1
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of the abelianized fundamental group of the Legendre/λ-family over the moduli stack; S_3 = SL_2(Z/2)-twist of the Fermat tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Ihara's and Anderson's work on Galois action on the Fermat tower; Nakamura; Deligne 1989

ideas.what: Fermat tower over moduli as an M_1-torsor F_∞(X̃/S), compatible with base change, unique up to unique isomorphism given the canonical map Π_{03}^∧ → M^∧
ideas.modern_name: Canonical torsor of tangential-base-point paths in the abelianized tower (Kummer torsor)

ideas.what: Geometric variant (next page): generalized Jacobian of an elliptic curve with modulus the 2-torsion divisor; its toric part R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m has Tate module M_1

missed.claim: Realizing the Fermat-tower Galois representation of π1(M_{1,1}/±1) via the torus R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m and the generalized Jacobian of an elliptic curve with modulus its 2-torsion. This is a family of semi-abelian varieties (1-motives) over the modular stack whose Tate-module extension class encodes the Fermat tower. Ihara/Anderson treat the Fermat tower over Q via Jacobi sums but, as far as I know, not as a 1-motive over the moduli of elliptic curves.
missed.quote: M_1(\tilde X/S) \overset{df}{=} M_0(\tilde X/S)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\hat{\mathbb Z}(1) ... (next page) J la jacobienne généralisée de X relative au diviseur de cette multisection
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a motivic (1-motive) model for part of the GT/modular action on the abelian layer of π1(P^1−3 pts). This could connect elliptic polylogarithm and mixed elliptic motive work (Hain–Matsumoto, Brown) with the Fermat/Ihara power series.

missed.claim: The question of finding a non-trivial geometric 'fibre type' on which G_{p,σ} acts, extending the modular homomorphism, is only begun here.
missed.quote: on voit que la tour de Fermat varie à ... sur tout schéma de base S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relates to finding geometric realizations of quotients of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action at the metabelian level.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients (Fermat tower, its S_3-twist, Tate modules of tori) are standard. Two things are a modestly interesting unpublished detail predating or parallel to Ihara–Anderson: the clean formulation of the Fermat tower as a canonical torsor varying over the moduli of elliptic curves mod ±1, and the proposed generalized-Jacobian model.
transcription_corrections: 'tore de Fermat' should read 'tour de Fermat' (tower), as on the next page.
'à symétrie pris' should read 'à symétrie près'.
'le Z-module constant tordu localement de rang deux': likely 'le Z-module constant tordu localement libre de rang deux' (or similar).
'revêtement [-étale-] des degrés trois' is probably 'revêtement de degré trois' (with 'deg' added); 'étale' appears struck.
Opening line reads 'M_{0,3} = N'_{1,1}' / 'M'_{1,1}' in the image; the second symbol is likely M'_{1,1}.
'pour iso et image inverse' is correct; 'a une section cartésienne d'une cat. fibrée ad hoc' is correct.
